content.text:
Lint was blocked by the sandbox permission prompt, so I couldn't run it — the change is one condition in existing style, and the test file follows the same patterns as its neighbors.

## Change

**`lib/decorate.js:124`** — `checkDependencies` now falls back to `hasInstanceProperty` when `checkExistence` misses:

```js
if (!checkExistence(instance, deps[i]) && !hasInstanceProperty(instance, deps[i])) {
  throw new FST_ERR_DEC_MISSING_DEPENDENCY(deps[i])
}
```

This is the fourth call site of the `hasInstanceProperty` helper added in #6753 (the other three being the `FST_ERR_DEC_ALREADY_PRESENT` guard in `decorateConstructor`, `checkRequestExistence` and `checkReplyExistence`). `hasInstanceProperty` walks the `parent` chain, so encapsulated plugins resolve too. The instance path (`decorate()` → plain Fastify instance) has no `instanceProperties`, so the added lookup returns `false` on the first iteration; and for ordinary dependencies `checkExistence` short-circuits it entirely.

**`test/decorator-instance-properties.test.js`** — five new cases: full built-in sets for `Request` (`id`, `params`, `raw`, `query`, `log`, `body`) and `Reply` (`raw`, `request`, `log`) as dependencies; an encapsulated plugin; a mixed built-in/user-decorator dependency array; and a regression case covering unknown dependencies plus a `Reply` decorator depending on the `Request`-only `params`.

## Verification

- With the fix: 11/11 pass in that file.
- With the one-line fix reverted: the four new positive cases fail, the rest pass — including the `FST_ERR_DEC_MISSING_DEPENDENCY` regression case, which holds both ways, confirming the fix didn't widen acceptance beyond constructor-assigned built-ins.

Per your instruction I ran only that one test file and did not commit.
